about: Vocabulary shared by every supported SQL dialect. Dialect files add to it and may replace an entry by repeating its name.

functions.name: COUNT
functions.summary: Counts rows, or the non-NULL values of an expression, in each group.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to count; NULLs are skipped. Use * to count every row, or DISTINCT expression to count unique values.

functions.name: SUM
functions.summary: Adds up the non-NULL values of a numeric expression in each group. Returns NULL when there are no non-NULL values.
functions.example: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id

signatures.returns: numeric (same family as the input, possibly widened)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The numeric value to total; NULLs are ignored. Prefix with DISTINCT to add each distinct value once.

functions.name: AVG
functions.summary: Returns the average of the non-NULL values of a numeric expression in each group. With integer input some engines return an integer; cast to a decimal type for a fractional result.
functions.example: SELECT AVG(CAST(price AS DECIMAL(10, 2))) FROM products

params.name: expression
params.doc: The numeric value to average; NULLs are ignored. Prefix with DISTINCT to average only distinct values.

functions.name: MIN
functions.summary: Returns the smallest non-NULL value of an expression in each group. Works on numbers, text and dates.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to compare; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: MAX
functions.summary: Returns the largest non-NULL value of an expression in each group. Works on numbers, text and dates.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to compare; NULLs are ignored.

functions.name: COALESCE
functions.summary: Returns the first of its arguments that is not NULL, or NULL if all of them are NULL. Arguments are evaluated left to right.

params.name: value1
params.doc: The first value to try.

params.name: value2
params.doc: The next value to try if the earlier ones are NULL; repeat for more fallbacks.

functions.name: NULLIF
functions.summary: Returns NULL when the two arguments are equal, otherwise the first argument. Often used to avoid division by zero.

params.name: value1
params.doc: The value returned when the two arguments differ.

params.name: value2
params.doc: The value that, when equal to value1, makes the result NULL.

functions.name: CAST
functions.summary: Converts a value to another data type. Raises an error when the value cannot be converted.

params.name: expression AS data_type
params.doc: The value to convert, the keyword AS, then the target data type, including any length or precision.

functions.name: UPPER
functions.summary: Returns a string with its letters converted to uppercase.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to convert.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.summary: Returns a string with its letters converted to lowercase.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to convert.

functions.name: ABS
functions.summary: Returns the absolute (non-negative) value of a number.

params.name: number
params.doc: The number whose sign is removed.

functions.name: ROUND
functions.summary: Rounds a number to a given number of decimal places, or to a whole number when the places are left out.

params.name: number
params.doc: The number to round.

params.name: decimals
params.doc: Decimal places to keep; a negative value rounds to the left of the decimal point. Defaults to 0 where it may be omitted; some engines require it.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.summary: Returns a string with every occurrence of a search string replaced by another string.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to search in.

params.name: search
params.doc: The substring to find.

params.name: replacement
params.doc: The text to put in place of each occurrence; an empty string deletes them.

functions.name: TRIM
functions.summary: Returns a string with leading and trailing spaces removed.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to trim.

functions.name: LTRIM
functions.summary: Returns a string with leading spaces removed.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to trim.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The set of characters to strip instead of spaces; not accepted by every engine.

functions.name: RTRIM
functions.summary: Returns a string with trailing spaces removed.

params.name: string
params.doc: The text to trim.

params.name: characters
params.doc: The set of characters to strip instead of spaces; not accepted by every engine.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time, written without parentheses. The exact type, precision and time zone handling depend on the engine.

functions.name: ROW_NUMBER
functions.summary: Numbers the rows of each window partition 1, 2, 3, … in the window's ORDER BY order, with no ties.
functions.example: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date)

functions.name: RANK
functions.summary: Ranks the rows of each window partition by the window's ORDER BY; tied rows share a rank and the next rank skips ahead (1, 1, 3).

functions.name: DENSE_RANK
functions.summary: Ranks the rows of each window partition by the window's ORDER BY; tied rows share a rank and no ranks are skipped (1, 1, 2).

functions.name: NTILE
functions.summary: Splits the ordered rows of each window partition into a number of groups as equal in size as possible and returns each row's group number, starting at 1.

params.name: buckets
params.doc: How many groups to split the rows into; must be a positive integer.

functions.name: LAG
functions.summary: Returns a value from a row that comes a given number of rows before the current row in the window's order, or a default when there is no such row.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to read from the earlier row.

params.name: offset
params.doc: How many rows back to look; defaults to 1.

params.name: default
params.doc: The value returned when the offset row falls outside the partition; defaults to NULL.

functions.name: LEAD
functions.summary: Returns a value from a row that comes a given number of rows after the current row in the window's order, or a default when there is no such row.

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to read from the later row.

params.name: offset
params.doc: How many rows ahead to look; defaults to 1.

params.name: default
params.doc: The value returned when the offset row falls outside the partition; defaults to NULL.

functions.name: FIRST_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns the value of an expression at the first row of the current window frame.
functions.example: FIRST_VALUE(price) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY valid_from)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to read from the frame's first row.

functions.name: LAST_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns the value of an expression at the last row of the current window frame. The default frame ends at the current row, so add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING to get the partition's last row.
functions.example: LAST_VALUE(price) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY valid_from ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)

params.name: expression
params.doc: The value to read from the frame's last row.

functions.name: PERCENT_RANK
functions.summary: Returns the relative rank of each row in its window partition as (rank - 1) / (rows - 1), a value from 0 to 1.

functions.name: CUME_DIST
functions.summary: Returns the cumulative distribution of each row in its window partition: the fraction of rows ordered at or before it, greater than 0 and at most 1.

keywords.name: SELECT
keywords.doc: Starts a query that returns rows.

keywords.name: FROM
keywords.doc: Names the tables, views, subqueries or joins a statement reads rows from.

keywords.name: WHERE
keywords.doc: Filters rows before grouping; only rows for which the condition is true are kept (false and unknown are dropped).

keywords.name: GROUP BY
keywords.doc: Groups rows that share values so aggregates are computed per group.

keywords.name: HAVING
keywords.doc: Filters groups after GROUP BY; the condition may use aggregates such as COUNT(*) > 1.

keywords.name: ORDER BY
keywords.doc: Sorts the result rows, or the rows of a window, by one or more expressions. Without it, row order is not guaranteed.

keywords.name: ASC
keywords.doc: Sorts in ascending order (smallest first). This is the default.

keywords.name: DESC
keywords.doc: Sorts in descending order (largest first).

keywords.name: DISTINCT
keywords.doc: Removes duplicate rows from a query's result, or duplicate values from an aggregate's input.

keywords.name: ALL
keywords.doc: Keeps duplicates (the default for SELECT and aggregates; UNION ALL keeps duplicate rows), or, after a comparison operator, requires the comparison to hold for every row of a subquery.

keywords.name: AS
keywords.doc: Gives a column, table or subquery an alias; also separates the value from the target type in CAST.

keywords.name: JOIN
keywords.doc: Combines rows from two tables using a join condition. A plain JOIN is an inner join.

keywords.name: INNER JOIN
keywords.doc: Returns only the pairs of rows from both tables that satisfy the join condition.
keywords.syntax: table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON condition

keywords.name: LEFT JOIN
keywords.doc: Returns every row of the left table, with matching right-table rows or NULLs where there is no match. Same as LEFT OUTER JOIN.
keywords.syntax: table1 LEFT [OUTER] JOIN table2 ON condition

keywords.name: RIGHT JOIN
keywords.doc: Returns every row of the right table, with matching left-table rows or NULLs where there is no match. Same as RIGHT OUTER JOIN.
keywords.syntax: table1 RIGHT [OUTER] JOIN table2 ON condition

keywords.name: FULL JOIN
keywords.doc: Returns every row of both tables, matched where the condition holds and padded with NULLs where it does not. Same as FULL OUTER JOIN; not supported by every engine.
keywords.syntax: table1 FULL [OUTER] JOIN table2 ON condition

keywords.name: CROSS JOIN
keywords.doc: Returns every combination of a row from the first table with a row from the second (the Cartesian product). Takes no join condition.

keywords.name: INNER
keywords.doc: Marks an inner join, which keeps only matching rows from both sides.

keywords.name: LEFT
keywords.doc: Marks a left outer join, which keeps every row of the left table.

keywords.name: RIGHT
keywords.doc: Marks a right outer join, which keeps every row of the right table.

keywords.name: FULL
keywords.doc: Marks a full outer join, which keeps every row of both tables.

keywords.name: OUTER
keywords.doc: Optional word in LEFT, RIGHT and FULL joins; unmatched rows are kept and padded with NULLs.

keywords.name: CROSS
keywords.doc: Marks a cross join, which pairs every row of one table with every row of the other.

keywords.name: ON
keywords.doc: Introduces a join condition; also names the table in statements such as CREATE INDEX and CREATE TRIGGER.

keywords.name: USING
keywords.doc: Joins on columns that have the same name in both tables, listing them once instead of writing an ON condition. Not supported by every engine; some also use USING in other statements.

keywords.name: UNION
keywords.doc: Combines the rows of two queries with matching column lists and removes duplicates. Use UNION ALL to keep them.

keywords.name: UNION ALL
keywords.doc: Combines the rows of two queries with matching column lists, keeping duplicates. Faster than UNION because no duplicate removal is needed.

keywords.name: INTERSECT
keywords.doc: Returns the distinct rows that appear in the results of both queries.

keywords.name: EXCEPT
keywords.doc: Returns the distinct rows of the first query that do not appear in the second.

keywords.name: INSERT
keywords.doc: Adds new rows to a table, from a VALUES list or a query.

keywords.name: INSERT INTO
keywords.doc: Adds new rows to the named table, from a VALUES list or a query. Columns left out of the list get their defaults.

keywords.name: INTO
keywords.doc: Names the target table of an INSERT; some engines also use it to send query results into a new table or variables.

keywords.name: VALUES
keywords.doc: Supplies literal rows, for an INSERT or as an inline row source.

keywords.name: UPDATE
keywords.doc: Changes column values in existing rows. Without a WHERE clause every row of the table is changed.
keywords.syntax: UPDATE table SET column = value [, …] [WHERE condition]

keywords.name: SET
keywords.doc: Lists the column assignments of an UPDATE; also starts statements that change session or engine settings.

keywords.name: DELETE
keywords.doc: Removes rows from a table. Without a WHERE clause every row is removed.

keywords.name: CREATE
keywords.doc: Creates a database object such as a table, view, index or trigger.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE | VIEW | INDEX | TRIGGER name …

keywords.name: ALTER
keywords.doc: Changes the definition of an existing database object, such as adding a column to a table.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE table ADD column type

keywords.name: DROP
keywords.doc: Permanently removes a database object and, for a table, all of its data.
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE | VIEW | INDEX | TRIGGER name

keywords.name: TABLE
keywords.doc: Names a table as the object of CREATE, ALTER, DROP and similar statements.

keywords.name: VIEW
keywords.doc: A stored query that can be selected from like a table.

keywords.name: INDEX
keywords.doc: A structure that speeds up lookups and sorting on one or more columns of a table.

keywords.name: UNIQUE
keywords.doc: A constraint or index option requiring that no two rows share the same values in the listed columns.

keywords.name: PRIMARY KEY
keywords.doc: The constraint that identifies each row of a table: its columns must be unique and not NULL. A table has at most one.

keywords.name: PRIMARY
keywords.doc: Part of PRIMARY KEY, the constraint that uniquely identifies each row of a table.

keywords.name: FOREIGN KEY
keywords.doc: A constraint requiring that values in the listed columns match a key in another table (or be NULL).

keywords.name: FOREIGN
keywords.doc: Part of FOREIGN KEY, a constraint that links columns to a key in another table.

keywords.name: KEY
keywords.doc: Part of PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY constraint definitions.

keywords.name: REFERENCES
keywords.doc: Names the table and columns a foreign key points to.

keywords.name: CHECK
keywords.doc: A constraint that rejects rows for which the condition is false.

keywords.name: DEFAULT
keywords.doc: The value a column gets when an INSERT does not supply one; also usable in VALUES and SET to request that value.

keywords.name: CONSTRAINT
keywords.doc: Gives a constraint a name so it can be referenced later, for example to drop it.
keywords.syntax: CONSTRAINT name PRIMARY KEY | FOREIGN KEY | UNIQUE | CHECK …

keywords.name: NOT
keywords.doc: Negates a condition. NOT of an unknown (NULL) condition is still unknown.
keywords.syntax: NOT condition | NOT IN | NOT EXISTS | NOT BETWEEN | NOT LIKE

keywords.name: AND
keywords.doc: True when both conditions are true. Also separates the bounds of BETWEEN.

keywords.name: OR
keywords.doc: True when either condition is true. AND binds tighter than OR, so use parentheses when mixing them.

keywords.name: IN
keywords.doc: True when a value equals any value in a list or subquery result. NOT IN with a NULL in the list is never true.

keywords.name: EXISTS
keywords.doc: True when the subquery returns at least one row.

keywords.name: BETWEEN
keywords.doc: True when a value lies within a range, including both bounds.

keywords.name: LIKE
keywords.doc: Matches text against a pattern where % matches any run of characters and _ matches one character. Case sensitivity depends on the engine and collation.

keywords.name: IS
keywords.doc: Tests for NULL: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL are the correct way to check for missing values, since = NULL is never true.

keywords.name: CASE
keywords.doc: Returns the result of the first WHEN branch that matches, else the ELSE value, else NULL.
keywords.syntax: CASE [expression] WHEN value_or_condition THEN result […] [ELSE result] END

keywords.name: WHEN
keywords.doc: Starts a branch of a CASE expression with the value or condition to test.

keywords.name: THEN
keywords.doc: Gives the result of a CASE branch when its WHEN matches.

keywords.name: ELSE
keywords.doc: Gives the result of a CASE expression when no WHEN branch matches; without it the result is NULL.

keywords.name: END
keywords.doc: Closes a CASE expression or a BEGIN … END block.

keywords.name: WITH
keywords.doc: Defines named subqueries (common table expressions) that the following statement can reference like tables.

keywords.name: OVER
keywords.doc: Turns a function into a window function, computed over a set of rows related to the current row without collapsing them.

keywords.name: PARTITION BY
keywords.doc: Splits the rows of a window into groups; the window function restarts for each group.

keywords.name: PARTITION
keywords.doc: Part of PARTITION BY in a window definition; some engines also use it for table partitioning.

keywords.name: BY
keywords.doc: Part of GROUP BY, ORDER BY and PARTITION BY.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY | ORDER BY | PARTITION BY expression

keywords.name: ROWS
keywords.doc: Defines a window frame by a count of physical rows before or after the current row.

keywords.name: RANGE
keywords.doc: Defines a window frame by value relative to the current row's ORDER BY value, so peer rows with equal values are included together.

keywords.name: PRECEDING
keywords.doc: A window frame bound a number of rows (or a value range) before the current row.

keywords.name: FOLLOWING
keywords.doc: A window frame bound a number of rows (or a value range) after the current row.

keywords.name: CURRENT ROW
keywords.doc: A window frame bound at the current row (with RANGE, at the current row's peers).
keywords.syntax: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW

keywords.name: CURRENT
keywords.doc: Part of CURRENT ROW in a window frame bound.

keywords.name: ROW
keywords.doc: Part of CURRENT ROW in a window frame bound; also used in trigger and row-value syntax.

keywords.name: UNBOUNDED
keywords.doc: A window frame bound at the first (PRECEDING) or last (FOLLOWING) row of the partition.

keywords.name: BEGIN
keywords.doc: Starts a transaction, or opens a block of statements closed by END. The exact form varies by engine.

keywords.name: COMMIT
keywords.doc: Makes the changes of the current transaction permanent.

keywords.name: ROLLBACK
keywords.doc: Undoes the changes of the current transaction, or only those made after a savepoint.

keywords.name: TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: A unit of work whose changes are committed or rolled back together. How one is started varies by engine.

keywords.name: SAVEPOINT
keywords.doc: Marks a point inside a transaction that can later be rolled back to without undoing the whole transaction. Some engines use a different statement for this.

keywords.name: TRIGGER
keywords.doc: Code that runs automatically when rows of a table are inserted, updated or deleted.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TRIGGER name {BEFORE | AFTER} {INSERT | UPDATE | DELETE} ON table …

keywords.name: ADD
keywords.doc: Adds a column or constraint to an existing table in ALTER TABLE.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE table ADD [COLUMN] column type

keywords.name: COLUMN
keywords.doc: Names a column in ALTER TABLE statements; optional in some engines.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE table ADD | DROP [COLUMN] column

keywords.name: ANY
keywords.doc: After a comparison operator, true when the comparison holds for at least one row of a subquery. Same as SOME; not supported by every engine.

keywords.name: SOME
keywords.doc: After a comparison operator, true when the comparison holds for at least one row of a subquery. Same as ANY; not supported by every engine.

keywords.name: ESCAPE
keywords.doc: Names the character that makes a following % or _ in a LIKE pattern match literally.

keywords.name: COLLATE
keywords.doc: Applies a collation, which sets how text is compared and sorted (case and accent sensitivity, language rules).

keywords.name: NATURAL
keywords.doc: Makes a join match on every column name the two tables share. Fragile if columns are added later; not supported by every engine.
keywords.syntax: table1 NATURAL [LEFT | RIGHT | INNER] JOIN table2

constants.name: NULL
constants.doc: The absence of a value. Compare with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL; = NULL is never true.
